questions.question_text:
Write the $x$- and $y$-intercepts of the line shown.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-1,xmax=4,ymin=-2,ymax=7,xtick={-1,0,1,2,3,4},ytick={-2,0,2,4,6},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,<->,domain=-0.3:2.6,samples=2] {-3*x+6};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Swapped the x- and y-intercept values with each other.
Wrote each intercept with its coordinates in the wrong order.
Attached each axis crossing to the wrong intercept.

questions.solution_text:
The line crosses the $x$-axis at $x=2$ and the $y$-axis at $y=6$.
$x$-intercept: $(2,0)$
$y$-intercept: $(0,6)$

questions.question_text:
Does the point $(1,5)$ lie on the line $y = 4x + 1$ shown?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-1,xmax=3,ymin=-3,ymax=8,xtick={-1,0,1,2,3},ytick={-2,0,2,4,6,8},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,<->,domain=-0.9:1.6,samples=2] {4*x+1};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Left out the $+1$ constant when substituting.
Subtracted the constant instead of adding it.
Substituted the y-value into x instead of the x-value.

questions.solution_text:
$y=4x+1$
$=4(1)+1$
$=5$
The line gives $y=5$ at $x=1$, which matches the point's $y$-value, so $(1,5)$ lies on the line.

questions.question_text: Find the $x$- and $y$-intercepts of the line $y = 3x - 9$ using its equation.

options.why: Read the constant as the x-intercept instead of solving $0=3x-9$.
Sign error solving $0=3x-9$, giving $x=-3$.
Swapped which intercept is the x- and which is the y-intercept.

questions.solution_text:
$y$-intercept: substitute $x=0$.
$y=3(0)-9$
$=-9$
The $y$-intercept is $(0,-9)$.
$x$-intercept: substitute $y=0$.
$0=3x-9$
$9=3x$
$x=3$
The $x$-intercept is $(3,0)$.

questions.question_text: Find the $x$- and $y$-intercepts of the line $y = 2x + 3$ using its equation.

options.why: Sign error solving $0=2x+3$, giving $x=1.5$.
Read the constant as the x-intercept without solving.
Swapped which intercept is the x- and which is the y-intercept.

questions.solution_text:
$y$-intercept: substitute $x=0$.
$y=2(0)+3$
$=3$
The $y$-intercept is $(0,3)$.
$x$-intercept: substitute $y=0$.
$0=2x+3$
$-3=2x$
$x=-1.5$
The $x$-intercept is $(-1.5,0)$.
